newsitem.title: USA: Ohio corn seeding two weeks ahead of average.
newsitem.headline: Ohio corn seeding two weeks ahead of average.

text.p: Rain slowed corn plantings in the week ended Sunday but 82 percent of the crop was seeded, about two weeks ahead of average, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop update.
About 11 percent had emerged versus nine percent on average.
"The corn crop has been slow to emerge due to cold soils but until this past week, no concerns had been raised about seed rotting in the ground." the report said.
"With surplus soil moisture at the highest level of the year and soil temperatures still below ideal, the potential for seed rotting has increased," it said.
Soil moisture was rated three percent short, 63 percent adequate and 34 percent surplus.
Soybeans were 39 percent seeded, more than double the five-year average of 14 percent.

Winter wheat was 64 percent jointed, against 55 percent average. The crop was rated three percent very poor, 12 percent poor, 35 percent fair, 40 percent good and 10 percent excellent, down slightly from the previous week.
Oats were rated six percent poor, 40 percent fair, 46 percent good and eight percent excellent. The crop was 96 percent seeded as of Sunday, ahead of average.
Pasture was rated three percent very poor, 10 percent poor, 36 fair, 44 percent good and seven percent excellent.
